title: Localization
body: A construct can name a destination and a position. The enzymes that change the cell use Cytosolic, Secreted, or Transmembrane. The position is a place on the body: one pole, the other pole, one side, the other side, both poles, or both sides. Many genes refuse a destination they cannot use, and some refuse a position tag entirely.

Position is what aims a motor, a flagellum, a pilus, or Taperin. Taperin stays in the cytosol and still takes a position: it pinches the end where it gathers. Flagellin builds filaments at the site it was sent to. A motor protein spins whatever shares that site.
